## In short

- **Answer:** a change of **`{python} signed(pooled["median"])`** from grid slot to finish (+ is places gained, − places lost; median of the simulated races; middle half `{python} span(*pooled["middle_half"])`, middle 80% `{python} span(*pooled["middle_80"])`).
- **How sure:** not backtested. The simulation is built from 2026 results so far.
- **What would make it wrong:** his grid slot (qualifying had not run, so it is simulated); a retirement (`{python} pct(pooled["retire"], 0)` chance); anything 2026 results do not capture, as there is no Singapore, weather or safety-car adjustment. Known gaps: round 16 arrived labelled "Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia" and which race it was is unresolved; a small sample of `{python} summary["starts"]` races.

## Answer

**Actual result (R`{python} sg.RACE_ROUND`, added after the race): `{python} sg.actual_text(actual)`.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Question** | How many positions will Alex Albon move relative to his starting position on the grid at the Singapore Grand Prix? |
| **Convention** | Grid slot minus classified finishing position. Starts 18th, finishes 19th = −1. Positive means places gained. |
| **Status** | Pre-race analysis. Qualifying had not run, so his grid slot is unknown and is simulated. The actual result is shown alongside. |
| **Prepared** | 2026-10-08 |
| **Data** | the local DuckDB file built by `uv run build`, 2026 rounds 1–`{python} sg.LAST_ROUND` |

## 1 · Type of analysis and why

Method: Monte Carlo simulation. The race is simulated `{python} count(sim.total_races)` times (`{python} sim.runs` runs of `{python} count(sim.races_per_run)`). Each simulated race draws every uncertain ingredient at random from real 2026 results, and the answer is read from where the outcomes pile up.

| Why a simulation, not a single formula | What it means here |
|---|---|
| The outcome is two different races in one | When Albon finishes he averages `{python} signed1(summary["mean_change_finished"])` places; when he retires, `{python} signed1(summary["mean_change_non_finished"])`. An average of the two describes a race that rarely happens. |
| His grid slot is unknown | Qualifying has not run and the starting slot changes the answer, so each simulated race draws a grid slot too. |
| Only `{python} summary["starts"]` races of evidence | The simulation carries that uncertainty through to the result instead of hiding it in one number. |

Three draws per simulated race:

| Draw | Source |
|---|---|
| 1 · Grid slot | His `{python} summary["starts"]` starting slots this season, recent races weighted more (weight halves every `{python} simulation.RECENCY_HALF_LIFE` races). |
| 2 · Retires or finishes | His record of `{python} summary["non_finishes"]` non-finishes in `{python} summary["starts"]` blended with the field rate of `{python} pct(summary["field_non_finish_pct"], 0)`, giving a `{python} pct(pooled["retire"], 0)` retirement chance that itself varies from race to race. |
| 3 · Places gained or lost | If he finishes: `{python} share(simulation.OWN_FINISH_SHARE)` of the draws from his own `{python} summary["finishes"]` finishes, the rest from other `{python} sg.SEASON` finishers who started within `{python} simulation.PEER_WINDOW` slots of him. If he retires: from 2026 retirements from a similar slot. |

## 3 · Simulation result

```{python}
#| label: fig-sg-outcomes
#| fig-cap: "Share of all simulated races at each outcome. Two overlapping shapes: finishes centred on small gains, retirements centred on losses."
figures.singapore_outcome_histogram(sim.histogram, pooled)
```

| Gains places | No change | Loses places | Retirement chance |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `{python} pct(pooled["gains"])` | `{python} pct(pooled["level"])` | `{python} pct(pooled["loses"])` | `{python} pct(pooled["retire"])` |

The lean toward a gain is weak. The most likely single outcomes sit close together: `{python} sg.top_outcomes_text(pooled)`. The most common change is `{python} signed(pooled["mode"])`. The median, `{python} signed(pooled["median"])`, is the estimate because it is the value with half of all outcomes on either side. Mean change `{python} signed(pooled["mean"])`; middle half `{python} span(*pooled["middle_half"])`; middle 80% `{python} span(*pooled["middle_80"])`.

## 6 · Caveats

- **Qualifying had not run.** Grid slot is the largest single input and is simulated, not known.
- **Round 16 is unresolved.** Jolpica returned a full round 16 result labelled "Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia", while the original calendar listed round 16 as Singapore on 2026-10-11. The base case includes it; excluding it keeps the median at `{python} signed(sim.scenario("Exclude round 16")["median"])`.
- **No Singapore-specific or weather adjustment.** Safety cars, rain and penalties are represented only to the extent they shaped 2026 results so far.
- **This is a pre-race estimate, not a computed answer.** The actual result above is read from `results` and shown for comparison; the simulation uses rounds 1–`{python} sg.LAST_ROUND` only.
